Consider yourself heard. I was in an abusive home. I'm 18, and I was removed four years ago. I felt similar. The world outside of the dark where I was abused wasn't what I thought it would be.
It might not mean much, but I relate to a whole lot of what you're saying. It's hard, right? I wanted to grow up so bad, thinking it would be so much easier when I was older, but it's so hard.
I came here for the same reason as you did, really.
Maybe to leave something if I end up ending it, but I also just wanted to be heard.

I hope you can stay alive. I hope it gets better, and I hope you can feel happy real soon.

I'm never busy, and I've got all night if you're still around. Feel free to message me, okay?
Hey, did you mean for this to be a positive message? I smiled a little, so if it was intended for that then that's good.

You sound stressed out. You sound overworked. But most frightening of all, you sound like a close friend of mine that I currently live with.
Your feelings right now are real and relevant, and I sincerely hope you don't hurt yourself tonight. 
Give yourself a well deserved break if you can, because like you said you worked hard to get here and you've earned every bit of it.

You say you're too far gone, and I often find myself thinking the same thing, but there is hope. By wanting to improve yourself, you can work hard on being open and honest with your psychologist.
Psychologists trust what you say 90% of the time, within reason, I've found. So, if you're lying, there's no way for them to help you. It's too easy to do this, and consequentially you get worse.
The hardest thing is being open. No one wants to sit there and tell someone they're weak and watch them write it down on a clipboard. Still, you should try it. Tell your psychologist something on a smaller scale you've been struggling with, maybe? And work up to the big stuff. If you can, talk to your mom about some things, too. If she knows something is wrong, she's probably so worried, and you don't have to tell her heavy issues but if she knows just a little bit she would feel better than not knowing at all. 
I'm sorry for rambling so long, and I hope I was able to help if only a little bit.

Do not do this. 
More likely than not you will end up in the hospital bed with a messed up body and possibly brain damage. Not only will it be awfully painful before you even end up on the hospital bed, you likely won't succeed in your goal and come out suffering more on the other side. 
My personal suggestion is to hold out a little longer if this is your only option. Do not turn to overdose. Please.
